blocks.prompt: 7. Find \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) by making suitable substitutions and applying the Chain Rule: \(y = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 + x}{1 - x}}\)
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein ek function doosre ke andar hai: bahar square root hai aur andar fraction \(\frac{1 + x}{1 - x}\). Aise function ko composite function kehte hain.
Diya kya hai? \(y = \sqrt{\frac{1 + x}{1 - x}}\). Find kya karna hai? \(\frac{dy}{dx}\), aur sawal khud keh raha hai: substitution aur chain rule se.
Rule kaunsa? Chain rule \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy}{du}\cdot\frac{du}{dx}\). Andar wale hisse ko \(u\) ka naam denge.
Plan: \(u\) rakhenge, \(\frac{dy}{du}\) power rule se, \(\frac{du}{dx}\) quotient rule se, dono multiply, phir jawab ko saaf karenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \sqrt{\frac{1 + x}{1 - x}}\), jahan \(-1 < x < 1\).
Maloom karna: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Tareeqa: chain rule. \(-1 < x < 1\) isliye ke root ke andar wali cheez positive honi chahiye aur \(x = 1\) par fraction toot jata hai.

Substitution karein
\[u = \dfrac{1 + x}{1 - x},\quad y = u^{1/2}\]
Kyun: mushkil andar wale hisse ko ek naam \(u\) de diya. Ab \(y\) sirf \(u\) ki ek seedhi power hai, jis ka derivative aasaan hai. Isi ko 'suitable substitution' kehte hain.

\(y\) ka derivative \(u\) ke respect se
\[\dfrac{dy}{du} = \tfrac{1}{2}u^{-1/2} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\]
Kyun: power rule, \(n = \frac{1}{2}\), power ek kam ho kar \(-\frac{1}{2}\).

\(u\) ka derivative \(x\) ke respect se
\[\dfrac{du}{dx} = \dfrac{(1)(1 - x) - (1 + x)(-1)}{(1 - x)^2}\]
\[= \dfrac{2}{(1 - x)^2}\]
Kyun: \(u\) fraction hai to quotient rule. \((1 + x)' = 1\), \((1 - x)' = -1\). Upar \(1 - x + 1 + x = 2\) bacha.
Dhyan dein: \((1 - x)' = -1\) hai; is minus ko bhoolne se upar \(-2x\) jaisi ghalat cheez aa jati hai.

Chain rule se jorein
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{u}} \cdot \dfrac{2}{(1 - x)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - x}{1 + x}} \cdot \dfrac{1}{(1 - x)^2}\]
Kyun: dono derivatives multiply kiye, 2 aur 2 cancel. \(u\) ko wapas \(x\) mein badla: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\) yani fraction ulta ho kar \(\sqrt{\frac{1 - x}{1 + x}}\). Jawab hamesha asal variable \(x\) mein dena hota hai.

Tasdeeq \(x = 0\) par
\[\dfrac{1}{(1)(1)} = 1\]
Kyun: \(x\) bohat chhota ho to \((1 + x)^{1/2} \approx 1 + \frac{x}{2}\) aur \((1 - x)^{-1/2} \approx 1 + \frac{x}{2}\); in ka product taqreeban \(1 + x\) hai, jis ka slope 1 hai. Formula bhi 1 de raha hai, to jawab sahi hai.
